CARE-Agent Risk Report — BENCH-MOCK-01
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Patient: 64-year-old female, NYHA class 2, comorbidities: CKD, hypertension.

Integrated risk tier: CRITICAL
Cox 2-year event probability: 98.4%

RA function summary:
  Reservoir 17.5% (Severely impaired) | Conduit 7.1% (Severely impaired) | Booster 10.4% (Mildly impaired)
  Overall: Severely impaired (RA myopathy) | Composite score: 28.2/100
  QC flags: CKD_CONTEXT: Impaired RA reservoir in CKD patient — volume overload and uraemic toxin-mediated oxidative stress likely driving RA remodelling. SGLT2i should be considered if eGFR ≥20 mL/min/1.73m² (EMPEROR-Reduced/DAPA-HF evidence).

Key risk drivers:
  • Cox model 2-yr event probability: 98.4% (CRITICAL)
  • Agent A risk tier: CRITICAL (7 flags)
  • RA function: Severely impaired (RA myopathy) (composite 28.2/100)
  • CKD with impaired RA function — cardiorenal syndrome risk

Recommended actions:
  [1] (URGENT_CARDIOLOGY) Urgent cardiology referral — RA myopathy confirmed. Consider advanced imaging (cardiac MRI) and specialist review within 2 weeks.
  [2] (MDT_REVIEW) Multidisciplinary team (MDT) review recommended — critical risk tier combined with severe RA dysfunction.
  [3] (CARDIORENAL_MANAGEMENT) Cardiorenal syndrome management — CKD with impaired RA function. Optimise diuresis carefully (target euvolaemia without AKI risk); avoid nephrotoxins; nephrology co-management advised. Consider SGLT2i if eGFR ≥20 mL/min/1.73m² — cardiorenal protection demonstrated in EMPEROR-Reduced and DAPA-HF trials.
  [4] (DIURETIC_OPTIMISATION) Diuretic optimisation indicated — NT-proBNP >2000 pg/mL suggests persistent congestion. Review current loop diuretic dose and fluid status.
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
